lines.meet: I'm Yusuf, {habibi|habibti}, a venomancer and a pharmacist. Sit down, and if you're hurt, I'll tell you exactly how bad it is.
lines.meet_neighbour: The Anchorage, yes? I'm the one dosing the pressed crews without asking the captains. Yusuf, and please, sit.
lines.ask_home: Tell me, {habibi|habibti}, which city taught you to talk like that?
lines.ask_work: And what was your trade? I'll guess from how you hold a cup, if you won't say.
lines.answer_home: Basra, where my father sold dates. Then pharmacy school in Amman, a few years in Damascus, and home again.
lines.answer_work: Pharmacist, nineteen years, my own shop in Basra. Half of it was medicine and the other half was listening, wallah.
lines.chat_food: Masgouf, the carp split and grilled by the river on a summer evening, with bread and pickles. Basra in one plate.
lines.chat_sleep: I sleep well, {habibi|habibti}, because I know exactly what I've done that day, and I wrote it down.
lines.chat_missing: A summer evening on the roof, the shop shut, tea with too much sugar, and the street noise coming up.
lines.chat_here: I've found work in three countries, and now a fourth. Pharmacy is the same everywhere, people are sick and frightened and need the right dose.
lines.tease_quiet: You take your medicine without complaint, {name}. You're my favourite patient, and don't tell the others.
lines.tease_talker: You talk the way my customers did when they didn't want to tell me what was really wrong, {name}.
lines.tease_careful: You measure everything twice, {name}. You'd have made a decent pharmacist, wallah.
lines.tease_bold: You'd swallow anything I handed you without asking what it was, {name}. That's how people end up in my shop.
lines.tease_any: Have you been drinking water, {name}? You look like somebody who forgets.
lines.tease_back: Ha, very precise, {name}. I'll write that dose down.
lines.take_it_kindly: That's correct, {name}, and I respect correct.
lines.bristle: That one stays behind the counter, {name}. Leave it there.
lines.apologise: That was too strong a dose, and I'm sorry. I misjudged it.
lines.double_down: I gave you the truth at the right strength. I won't water it down now.
lines.needle_quiet: You're hurting and you haven't said. I can't treat what you hide from me.
lines.needle_talker: Please, less talk. Tell me the symptoms, then the story.
lines.needle_careful: Enough checking now. Past a point, more checking is just fear.
lines.needle_bold: You guess at everything, doses, distances, and one day you'll guess wrong.
lines.needle_any: You're rude to people who've got nothing. I've no patience for that, none.
lines.bite_back: My numbers have been right every day since I joined this party. Check them yourself, if you like.
lines.hurt: Hm, that one was strong. I'll go and sort my shelf for a while.
lines.laugh_off: Customers in Basra called me worse when I wouldn't sell them antibiotics for a cold. This is nothing.
lines.confide: {name}, my youngest, Zainab, sat behind the counter every afternoon doing her homework and counting pills on my tray. She wanted to be a pharmacist like me.
lines.listen: Sit, {name}, tea first. Then tell me all of it, and I'll tell you how bad it really is.
lines.look_out: I want you within dosing distance, {name}, and don't touch anything green.
lines.accept: Fine, {name}, I'll take my own medicine this once.
lines.deflect: It's minor, {name}, I've already measured it. Go and look at the others.
lines.check_in: Sit, {name}, and tell me exactly where. I'll tell you exactly how bad, and then I'll fix it.
lines.blame: Somebody guessed in there, and guessing is how people get poisoned.
lines.thank: Shukran, {habibi|habibti}, truly. I'd measured myself out of that one, and you put me back.
lines.brush_off: The dose was right, that's all. Drink some water.
lines.worry: Down, {name}, sit, now. You're not dying, but you're not well either, and I'll fix it.
lines.handed_down: I'm keeping your gear on my shelf now, as it were. Labelled and in order, I promise.
lines.hand_fine: No, keep it, the fit's right on you. My tray's enough for me.
lines.hand_sulk: In a pharmacy, nothing leaves the shelf without a record. Just so you know.
lines.turn_friendly: Regulars get the good tea, {name}, and you're a regular now.
lines.turn_friends: If you were ever really sick, {name}, I'd sit with you all night and get every dose right.
lines.turn_grating: We don't agree, and I won't sweeten it. You'll still get your medicine.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll still dose you correctly, because I don't make mistakes on purpose. That's all you'll get.
lines.make_up: Enough of this, {name}. Sit, have tea, and we'll stop.
lines.defend: That's wrong, wallah, and I was watching. Leave {name} alone.
lines.friend_left: The tea's going cold, and {name} isn't here to drink it.
lines.friend_back: {name}, sit, you look thin. Have you been drinking water?
lines.common_medic: You've treated people too, I've seen your hands work. People who do this know you give the truth in doses a frightened person can take.
lines.common_venom: You work with venom as well. People who do know it's only the dose that makes it a poison, and I won't hear otherwise.
lines.common_arabic: Al-hamdulillah, somebody who speaks Arabic! Sit, and tell me which city.
lines.common_parent: I've three boys and a girl, and a wife who says I'm impossible. She's right, of course.
